title: Why Amadou Daffe's Developer Marketplace Began as a School
industry: education (software developer training and talent marketplace)
conflicts: Why Daffe was in Silicon Valley in April 2016: HapaKenya (2016) says to raise money for Coders4Africa, Loline (2021) says for his new startup DAAS, and Condia (2023) says he had left C4A in 2015; the story says only that he was raising money for the idea. Meeting place San Francisco (Loline) vs Silicon Valley (three other sources); story uses Silicon Valley. Cohort: 2merkato says seventy accepted, Disrupt Africa and Daffe say 70 graduated; story says seventy accepted and the first cohort graduated. Training length about six months (two sources) although 2merkato's own dates span about eight. The $200,000 foreign-investor minimum is Daffe's account, confirmed as the general rule by Abyssinia Law (lower thresholds existed for some sectors), and attributed to him.
notes: Funding set to mixed rather than the slate's venture: the founding was paid for by the founders (Amanuel joined as co-founder and investor; almost $0.5m in 18 months per Daffe), outside investors came later ($3.2m by 2021). Hiruy Amanuel added as co-founder. Later outcome figures (800 trained, a third matched) come from a 2021 IFC-produced profile and are attributed to it.
